title: Naga Council Issues 48-Hour Ultimatum Over Severed Head as Manipur Clashes Kill Nine
excerpt: The Joint Tribes Council Manipur demands the return of Ajinbou R's severed head within 48 hours after a weekend of Kuki-Naga clashes killed nine people across three hill districts.
body:
• The Joint Tribes Council Manipur has issued a "non-negotiable" 48-hour ultimatum demanding the return of the severed head of Ajinbou R, 52, allegedly beheaded in a militant attack on Makui Ashang village in Kangpokpi district. No post-mortem will be allowed until the head is returned for a dignified burial.
  • Nine people were killed in separate firing incidents in Kamjong, Ukhrul and Kangpokpi districts on Friday and Saturday. The spiral began with the shooting of a 22-year-old mother of five in Chassad village, which set off an exchange of fire between Kuki and Naga armed groups.
  • A video purportedly showing Ajinbou R's head among camouflaged, heavily armed militants went viral on Saturday. The council held the state and Central governments directly responsible for the renewed violence, calling the killing "an affront to humanity" and warning of the "most stringent measures".
  • Chief Minister Y Khemchand Singh condemned the killings, directed authorities to take immediate steps to restore order, and ordered additional security forces into Kangpokpi and Kamjong districts.

A 48-hour deadline over a severed head

On Sunday, the Working Committee of the Joint Tribes Council Manipur said the head of Ajinbou R remained missing and his body — taken to the Jawaharlal Nehru Institute of Medical Sciences in Imphal on Sunday night — would not be examined until the head was returned. "We will not allow state machinery to mutilate the remains further while his head is treated as a trophy by militants," the council said in its statement.

The council issued what it called a "non-negotiable 48-hour ultimatum" to locate and return the severed head, warning of the "most stringent measures" if the deadline passed without justice.

"The head of Ajinbou R remains missing. Post-mortem will not be conducted till his head is returned to his family members for a dignified burial."

— Joint Tribes Council Manipur, in a statement

How three days of violence unfolded

The fresh round of killings began on Friday night, when unidentified assailants shot dead a 22-year-old woman — a mother of five — in Chassad village in the Kuki-dominated, Naga-majority Kamjong district, according to news agency PTI. Her killing set off an exchange of fire between Kuki and Naga armed groups that continued into Saturday morning. A 42-year-old man was killed, 10 houses were torched, and prohibitory orders under Section 162 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita were imposed in the village.

On Saturday, suspected militants attacked Tapon and Makui villages in Kangpokpi district, killing two Naga village guards — M Daimai and R Gangmei — and another villager identified as Ringkangmai; the council says Ajinbou R was beheaded during this attack.

Elsewhere on Saturday, suspected militants shot dead 35-year-old Ngachanso Ningshen and 48-year-old Leishishan Leishadang in Ningchou village near the India-Myanmar border — locals told officials the attackers fled toward Myanmar — while 40-year-old Sandeep Rai was shot dead in his car near Chepu Yaolen village in Ukhrul district. Heavy exchanges of fire were also reported at Makui Ashang and Tapon.

Context & Background

This is a new Kuki-Naga front in a state already scarred by ethnic conflict. More than 40 people have been killed and dozens of houses torched in violence between Kuki and Naga tribes since February, according to PTI — the council's own tally is 32 Naga deaths since February. An earlier Meitei-Kuki ethnic conflict killed over 300 people, left 49 missing and rendered thousands homeless.

The council blamed Kuki armed groups — naming the KNF-P, KRA, KNA-MC, KNF-N and KNA-B — and said the government's Suspension of Operations framework "has not prevented violence; it has enabled it," demanding that militants return to designated camps and surrender illegal arms.

Impact & Analysis

The beheading and the viral video mark a grim escalation, and the council's ultimatum — backed by a threat of the "most stringent measures" — raises the risk of retaliatory mobilisation. With attackers reportedly fleeing toward Myanmar after the Ningchou shooting, the cross-border dimension complicates any security response.

Chief Minister Y Khemchand Singh condemned the killings, directed authorities to take "immediate and effective steps" to restore order, and urged all communities to prioritise "peace, dialogue and harmony". Additional forces have been rushed to Kangpokpi and Kamjong.

What's Next

The council's 48-hour clock runs out on Tuesday. Whether the severed head is recovered — and whether the ultimatum triggers wider retaliation — will decide if this flare-up stays contained or hardens into a longer confrontation. Watch for the government's answer to the probe demand and any movement on the SoO framework. PTI's full account of the killings is carried by the Nagaland Post, and further details on the ultimatum are at News89.
